entities.summary:
The President of Angola was a public office in Angola, a significant occurrence during the Classical era.

This office was created by the colonial powers in the 19th century, specifically in 1885, when Angola was divided among European powers.

The President of Angola played a crucial role in the country's transition to independence, with Agostinho Neto being the first president of the newly independent nation in 1975.

The office has continued to shape the country's politics, with José Eduardo dos Santos serving as president for nearly four decades.

The legacy of the President of Angola can be seen in the country's development, from the 1970s nationalization of industries to the 2000s oil-fueled economic growth.
